name: Subcision

lead: Subcision is a minor procedure in which a needle is inserted beneath the skin to cut the fibrous bands tethering a depressed scar, most often rolling acne scars. The payoff is a smoother skin surface as the scar lifts.

Releasing the scar creates a pocket where blood collects and collagen forms, which proponents say raises the scar. The term was coined in a 1995 paper describing a tri-beveled hypodermic needle. Studies include case series and small trials, and reviews list it within multimodal acne scar treatment.

paras: A clinician numbs the area and works the needle beneath each scarred zone, often in a series of sessions and combined with other scar treatments such as lasers or microneedling. Swelling and bruising settle over days, and collagen-related improvement is judged over following weeks to months.

Procedure-specific risks are not detailed in the sources reviewed, though bruising and swelling are expected from needle work under the skin. Medical sources describe subcision as in-office; do-it-yourself versions circulate in forums, where claims about results are anecdotal.

angle.text: Subcision is a clinic procedure that releases the fibrous bands pulling down rolling acne scars, so they lift and the skin surface looks smoother. Evidence consists of case series and small trials.

lead: Subcision is a minor procedure in which a needle is inserted beneath the skin to release fibrous bands tethering a depressed scar, most often rolling acne scars. The term was coined in a 1995 paper describing a tri-beveled hypodermic needle introduced through a puncture [1][2].

Proponents say releasing the scar lets the skin rise and stimulates collagen. Studies include case series and small trials, and general reviews list it within multimodal acne scar treatment [3][4][5].

paras: Acne scars are classified as icepick, rolling and boxcar [1]. Rolling scars are broad with a wave-like pattern, and subcision targets those held down by tethering [6]. Wikipedia describes blood pooling beneath the released area, raising the scar over time, and notes subsequent laser, peels or microdermabrasion are sometimes used [6].

A 2005 report described technique and outcomes in 40 patients [7]. Reviews place subcision alongside microneedling, peels and lasers, often in combination [3][4][5][8][9]. Wikipedia reports effectiveness for glabellar lines is debatable [6].

Forum users on looksmax.org discuss subcision as an option for tethered scars, with some reporting improved skin texture; at least one thread presents a do-it-yourself approach [10][11]. Dermatology sources describe it as a clinician-performed procedure.

Registered trials compare subcision with or alone against CO2 laser, platelet-rich plasma, exosomes, suction, cannula versus needle technique, and other combinations [12][13][14][15], and cellulite studies exist [16][17].

lore.intro: Subcision is discussed on looksmax.org as a step for tethered atrophic scars, sometimes after other treatments [10][11].

claims.claim: Subcision works for tethered scars better than microneedling or laser.
It can be done at home.
